status_summary: Legislation that tracks the Mandate's codification recommendation has cleared committee in both chambers but has not passed either. H.R. 740, the Veterans' ACCESS Act of 2025 (introduced 2025-01-28), was ordered reported as amended by voice vote by the House Veterans' Affairs Committee on 2025-07-23, its latest action, with no floor action and no committee report listed in GovInfo bill status. S. 275 (introduced 2025-01-28) had a Senate Veterans' Affairs Committee hearing on 2025-03-11 and was ordered reported favorably with an amendment in the nature of a substitute on 2025-07-30, its latest action. VA's regulation at 38 CFR 17.4040 still states the 2019 access standards (30 minutes and 20 days for primary, mental health and extended care; 60 minutes and 28 days for specialty care), and no veterans bill of rights or Secretarial directives on the six MISSION Act sections the Mandate lists were found; VA's community-care-related rules since 2025-01-20 (emergency-treatment notification, published 2026-07-10, and rescission of old Veterans Choice Program rules, published 2026-07-28) do not change the standards.

timeline.event: Sen. Moran introduces S. 275, the Veterans' ACCESS Act of 2025, referred to the Senate Veterans' Affairs Committee; it codifies drive-time and wait-time standards and requires written eligibility notice within two business days.
Rep. Bost, chairman of the House Veterans' Affairs Committee, introduces the House version, H.R. 740, with the same access standards and notice provisions.

The House Veterans' Affairs Committee holds a markup and orders H.R. 740 reported, as amended, by voice vote, one of 25 bills advanced that day; no committee report or floor action follows in the bill status record.
The Senate Veterans' Affairs Committee orders S. 275 reported favorably with an amendment in the nature of a substitute, after a hearing held 2025-03-11 (S.Hrg. 119-35).

Rep. Patronis introduces H.R. 8737, the Never Fight Alone Act: mental health access standards no more restrictive than specialty care, and a requirement that a joint resolution be enacted before most later changes to community care access standards or eligibility criteria take effect.
VA finalizes a rule expanding its process for 72-hour notification of emergency treatment (community-care-related; does not change access standards).
VA rescinds outdated Veterans Choice Program regulations.

title: Codify MISSION Act community care access standards and issue implementing directives
uncertainties: Bill status for H.R. 740 and S. 275 was read in GovInfo BILLSTATUS files; neither lists a committee report number, so whether reported prints were filed was not verified. The House committee vote method (voice vote) is confirmed by BILLSTATUS. The cosponsor counts (88 active for H.R. 740, 15 for S. 275) come from the researcher's reading of BILLSTATUS and were partly re-checked (15 for S. 275). The Federal Register citations and effective dates of the two 2026 VA rules (91 FR 42670 and 91 FR 47141) rest on the researcher's Federal Register API check and were not re-read in this review. VA directives and memoranda implementing MISSION Act sections are not published in the Federal Register, so none being found is weak evidence. The House committee ranking member's opposition rests on a newsletter account.
